object: funerary stela of sandstone, thick, rounded top with a winged disk, ten lines between rules
site: Amâra (Pezeme), found with an old woman at Amâra by F. W. Green, December 1909; taken to Halfa for the Sudan Government collection
notes: 47 x 22.5 cm; late style; copy from Blackman's squeezes compared with Green's sketch; Pl. VII (another copy: Sayce, P.S.B.A. xxxii, Pl. xl). Griffith: 'Azemeqê, born of Qêqaye, begotten of Amani-tame, sashimete of Ammon'; the names of Isis and Osiris carry rare additions (his p. 59); the terminal formulae are B, A 'of ordinary type but very rarely in this reversed order'; Azeme may be connected with the city name Pezeme; the winged disk is rare on Meroitic funerary stelae. As printed: q where later texts have w in qetNyiNli and qetrri; eri(6)kelowi has no initial t; both formulae have the c-shaped x (ḫ) in mxe, not X; [:?] is Griffith's bracketed, queried divider. Words split by his superscript line numbers are joined (qo(4)q^ye is his Qêqaye).
